## The Spirit of MIDSEA

**MIDSEA is a family of sorts.** Not one defined by blood, passports, or institutional affiliations, but by shared experiences, friendships, and perhaps some resonance of souls. Southeast Asian at heart, but never restricted by where one comes from.
We take our science seriously, but rarely ourselves. Come to one of our events, and chances are there will be karaoke somewhere. Beyond workshops and scientific discussions, it is the meals, laughter, late-night conversations, and friendships that hold us together.

Most of us are early-career researchers, still navigating uncertain futures, limited resources, and the occasional struggle to simply survive. Yet we believe that nurturing others is not something we must wait to do until we have established ourselves. 
**We grow by helping one another grow, even when we are still figuring things out ourselves.**
And we have been doing much of this on shoestring budgets. Our flagship MIDSEA Summer School has run largely on registration contributions from both participants *and instructors*, with generous help from kind allies over the years. Much of everything else happens through volunteered time, shared resources, and whatever each of us can bring to the table. It is not always sustainable, nor should it be romanticised. But it says something about how much people care for this community.
Our Community of Modellers for Peer Advice, Support & Skills (COMPASS) program formalizes this peer-caring. For example, we organize virtual spaces to practice presentations such as PhD viva or fellowship interviews to seek feedback and help from peer MIDSEA members. Peer-to-peer mentorships between people who face experiences slightly before another to share tips is also common practice.


## Philosophy and Governance

**A Community That Belongs to Its Members.** MIDSEA has never been particularly fond of rigid hierarchies. We value shared ownership over tightly controlled structures, even if that sometimes means a fair amount of chaos.
People like Alex, Pan (Wirichada), and Jomar are deeply respected, not merely because of their career stages, but because of the love, time, and devotion they have poured into this community. Yet respect should not mean that the future of MIDSEA rests in the hands of a few.

Of course, chaos alone doesn't get things done. Decisions have to be made, responsibilities taken, and things moved forward. We are still experimenting with how to make decisions decisively while keeping the process transparent and open to questions, disagreements, and concerns, regardless of one's seniority, nationality, or history with MIDSEA.

## Taskforces

As MIDSEA grows, and relationships and trust deepen, it's time to introduce *some* structure. Not to centralise control, but rather **to keep ownership distributed, information flowing, and opportunities open to everyone.**
We are experimenting with taskforces as spaces where members can take initiative, share responsibilities, and make things happen together. Each has a convener to keep things moving and senior advisors to lend their experience, but neither should become a gatekeeper.

## Membership

MIDSEA has been organic since its inception in 2022. We are now migrating towards a defined membership body to deepen our sense of community and help us create safe, effective spaces that support the growth of every member. Apply to be a member through our [MIDSEA Network Membership and Engagement Form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeATlRD16rUzF7yZF3K21D6to7IansdXqsgY0nzTd-I4XDVNg/viewform){target="_blank"}.
Criteria for admission is in the works. But for now, its resonance of souls and sharing of the MIDSEA Spirit.
